subject: Retention & redaction: PHI handling for Acme pilot
messages:
From: Dr. Emma Sorensen <dr.emma@acmehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Privacy Team <privacy@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: PHI retention and redaction questions for pilot

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and privacy leads have a short list of operational questions as we scope the pilot — specifically around retention limits and redaction behavior when PHI is ingested via our clinical chat integration. Key asks:

- Minimum and maximum retention windows you support for hosted vs. private deployments (we prefer 30 days for transcripts but need options down to 0-days for some fields).
- Mechanisms for field-level redaction vs. full-record deletion (are deletions truly removed from backups/snapshots?).
- How KV/prefix caches are handled — e.g., if a patient identifier appears in a recent inference cache, is that flushed on delete?
- Audit evidence we can include in our HIPAA binder (deletion logs, KMS key rotation, proof of backup purge).

I attached a short questionnaire (security_question_list.pdf) — would appreciate a point-by-point. Can we aim for a reply by next Tuesday?

Regards,
Emma
Dr. Emma Sorensen
VP, Clinical Ops — Acme Health
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Emma Sorensen <dr.emma@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PHI retention and redaction questions for pilot

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. I put together concise answers to help your legal/privacy review and attached a redaction matrix (redaction_matrix_v1.xlsx). High-level:

1) Retention windows (hosted / dedicated / private)
- Hosted (Redwood API): configurable per-tenant retention windows from 0 days to 3650 days. Default 90 days for transient request logs; customer can request 0-day retention for request bodies and model I/O (we put a hold and sign an addendum for 0-day policy).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): similar control but retention of platform-level traces/metrics may be 30 days by default; we can scope a contract to reduce trace retention.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customers control persistence — Redwood agents will configure deletion jobs to meet a specified retention SLO. On-prem deployments can enforce immediate purge of application DBs on request.

2) Redaction vs deletion
- Field-level redaction: we support automated redaction rules (regex, schema-based) at ingestion and a downstream redaction pipeline that overwrites fields in our object store with a redacted token. This is reversible only if you keep a separate re-identification key (we do not keep that key by default).
- Full-record deletion: issues a removal across the live store; background job also marks the record for removal from snapshot indices. Live deletion is immediate from primary stores; snapshot/backups follow the backup retention policy (see backups note).

3) Backups and snapshots
- Backups: incremental backups are retained according to your retention policy. We offer a 30-day default backup retention; shorter windows can be contracted. For strict 0-day deletion guarantees including backups, we recommend Private deployment with customer-controlled backups or a Hosted addendum that sets a short backup lifecycle and off-cycle purge.

4) Caches (KV / prefix caches)
- KV caches are in-memory on serving nodes with persistent write-through disabled for transient traces. On deletion request we invalidate the KV entries across the cluster — invalidation is propagated within seconds, and stale entries are not persisted in the primary object store. For additional safety, we run a soft TTL purge and immediate cache invalidation on any deletion API call.

5) Audit and evidence
- We provide append-only deletion logs, signed with KMS, that record deletion requests, operator/service identity, and S3 object tombstone ops. For Hosted and Dedicated we can provide a downloadable audit bundle (JSON lines) for the requested window. For Private, customers can route logs to their SIEM.

6) Practical recommendation for Acme pilot
- Keep conversational transcripts for 30 days with PII/PHI fields redacted at ingestion (names, MRNs, SSNs). Store redaction policy in a config file under your tenant and snapshot policy. If you need guaranteed zero-retention for certain PHI fields after the call, we recommend tokenization at the client side (replace with instrumented token) + Private deployment or Hosted addendum.

If you want, Monica (cc'd) can add compliance evidence details and we can schedule a 30-minute follow-up with engineering to demonstrate a deletion request in a staging tenant.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Emma Sorensen <dr.emma@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PHI retention and redaction questions for pilot

Hi Emma — adding a few compliance-oriented clarifications to Logan's excellent summary:

- Deletion SLO definition: for Hosted customers we offer a documented deletion lifecycle: live-store delete (T0), background index sweep (T0 + 1h), backup tombstone/mark for purge (depends on backup window) and final backup purge within configured backup retention window. Typical SLOs: live-store delete immediate; index sweep within 1–4 hours; backup purge within 30 days unless contracted down.

- Proofs for HIPAA binder:
  - Deletion logs (signed) — we can export per-record XID and timestamp.
  - KMS key rotation logs — showable via our KMS integration report.
  - Backup lifecycle report — showing backup creation and purge timestamps.
  - KV/cache invalidation events — stored as short-lived traces; we can export invalidation confirmations from the serving runtime.

- When 0-day retention is requested for certain fields, we advise doing one of the following to meet strict compliance:
  1) Client-side redaction/tokenization before transmission (strongest guarantee).
  2) Immediate server-side field redaction on ingest + Private deployment so backups are controlled by you.

- Edge case: If you use third-party integrations (analytics, SIEM) that mirror payloads, those copies must be included in your deletion scope — we can help map outbound hooks.

I uploaded a short guidance doc to the Drive link in the thread and attached a redaction matrix with recommended regex and example records. Let us know if you want a canned audit bundle for a sample deletion event.

Monica
Compliance Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Dr. Emma Sorensen <dr.emma@acmehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Acme Privacy Team <privacy@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-11T10:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PHI retention and redaction questions for pilot

Thanks Logan/Monica — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our privacy team after reviewing the matrix: 

- If we elect server-side redaction, can you provide a reproducible proof that the original value was overwritten (not just marked)? Our binder reviewers want the chain-of-custody for changes.
- How do you handle legal hold scenarios where records must be preserved but isolated? Is there an immutable snapshot option we can toggle with ACLs?
- For KV cache invalidation, can you provide a sample invalidation log entry?

I've attached a short screenshot of our security team's question set (acme_qs_screenshot.png). We still hope to keep default retention at 30 days for transcripts but need to lock down the 0-day option for MRN and SSN fields.

Emma
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Emma Sorensen <dr.emma@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T16:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PHI retention and redaction questions for pilot

Emma — quick responses and next steps: 

- Proof of overwrite: our redaction pipeline writes an audit event containing: record XID, field path, pre-redaction merkle hash (SHA-256) of the original field, post-redaction merkle hash, operator id, and timestamp. You can verify that the pre-redaction hash appears in the audit log and that the live store now contains the redacted token value. We can include sample audit bundle for one test deletion (we'll sign it with our KMS key).

- Legal hold / immutable snapshot: we offer an immutable snapshot option for enterprise contracts (snapshots that are write-once and retained under a legal-hold flag). Those snapshots are stored in a separate bucket with ACLs and require an authorized release. For the pilot, we can simulate an isolated snapshot and provide access controls.

- KV invalidation log sample: yes — sample entries include node id, key-hash, invalidate request id, origin service, and timestamp. I can export a redacted sample log (no PHI) — Monica, can you pull the sample and drop it in the Drive link?

Action items:
- Monica: prepare a canned audit bundle (1 test deletion) and the KV invalidation sample.
- Emma: confirm the list of exact fields you want 0-day for (MRN, SSN noted).
- Logan/Vivek: schedule a 30-min demo next week showing an ingestion -> redaction -> deletion cycle in staging.

If that plan works I'll prepare a short addendum we can sign to lock the backup retention to 30 days and field-level 0-day behavior for the specified fields.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redaction_matrix_v1.xlsx (see previous), security_question_list.pdf (from Emma)
